pages.text: Deuterium and tritium fuse when their ions are hot enough to get close: around 10-20 keV. A plasma of density n at temperature T loses its energy over a confinement time τ, which grows with the magnetic field holding it (here τ ∝ B²). It ignites when the Lawson triple product nTτ passes 3×10²¹ keV·s/m³. The plasma's pressure pushes on the field; past β = 5% of the magnetic pressure, it disrupts.
$(thing)Set$(): Plasma density, Ion temperature, Toroidal field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Edge turbulence: the confinement time varies by ±5%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The plasma has disrupted: its pressure beat the field; The superconducting coils have quenched (too much field); The superconducting coils are too warm.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Power follows the triple product.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Energy confinement time: τ ∝ B²$(br)Triple product: nTτ$(br)Plasma beta: β = 2μ₀nkT/B²
